question: When the input unit is wrong, how loudly does it fail — and how wrong is the answer?
contract: orbit 19 descending, identical cubes, identical model (OlmoEarth v1 Base), only the unit changes

db.input_unit_recorded: gamma0 dB (10*log10 of RTC linear power)

linear.input_unit_recorded: RAW LINEAR POWER — deliberately wrong, M97 control

agreement_between_units.reading: the two unit choices agree on 0 of 6 top windows

how_silent: The wrong unit raises no exception, ranks all 56 windows, and produces scores and a threshold inside the same plausible range as the correct unit. Nothing in the output signals the error. This is what made M75 publishable before it was caught.
claim_boundary: One contract, one model, one event. This measures the silence of the failure and the size of the resulting error here; it does not establish how large the error would be on other tasks. Not damage, not risk.
